The name Malkior is a reminder of the ultimate King and Ruler of the universe, and inspires us to live in accordance with His will.

historical_references.reference: Malkior was a heretic bishop during the early Christian era, who denied the divinity of Christ and held Arian beliefs. He is mentioned in the works of St. Augustine of Hippo.
historical_references.context: Arianism was a movement that rejected the doctrine of the Trinity and denied the divinity of Christ.

historical_references.reference: Malkior was a Frankish nobleman who converted to Christianity in the late 7th century AD and became a bishop. He was excommunicated by Pope Sergius I due to his involvement in political intrigues.
historical_references.context: Political intrigues and power struggles were common in the early medieval Christian Church.

He is known to manipulate and deceive mortals, often using their own weaknesses and ambitions against them. Malkior's true form is rarely seen, and his servants often use disguises to infiltrate human societies. His influence extends to various dark practices, including necromancy, ritual magic, and diabolism. His dark and complex nature continues to captivate audiences across multiple platforms, providing endless opportunities for rich storytelling and exploration.
